quarterly_data.signal: Ziihera approval release: the FDA has granted zanidatamab three Breakthrough Therapy designations - as a single agent for previously treated HER2 gene-amplified biliary tract cancer (BTC), with fluoropyrimidine- and platinum-containing chemotherapy with or without tislelizumab for first-line HER2+ GEA, and for previously treated HER2+ colorectal cancer (CRC) - and two Fast Track designations (single agent in refractory BTC; with standard-of-care chemotherapy in first-line GEA), plus FDA Orphan Drug designations for BTC, gastric (including GEJ) and esophageal cancer and matching European Medicines Agency Orphan Drug designations. Continued approval in BTC may be contingent on a confirmatory trial. Ziihera is also approved in the European Union and other countries, is developed by Jazz and BeOne Medicines under license agreements from Zymeworks, and HERIZON-GEA-01 remains ongoing with additional analyses planned.
quarterly_data.figure: three FDA Breakthrough Therapy designations; two FDA Fast Track designations; FDA and EMA Orphan Drug designations for BTC, gastric/GEJ and esophageal cancer

quarterly_data.signal: Ziihera first-line GEA label safety data: with chemotherapy and tislelizumab, diarrhea was reported in 85% of 330 patients in clinical studies (Grade 3 24%, Grade 4 2.1%; fatal outcomes 1.5%), serious adverse reactions occurred in 59% of 294 HERIZON-GEA-01 patients, fatal adverse reactions in 2.4% and permanent discontinuation of Ziihera in 13%; with chemotherapy alone, diarrhea was reported in 81% of 395 patients in clinical studies (Grade 3 20%, Grade 4 1.3%), serious adverse reactions occurred in 49% of 305 patients and permanent discontinuation in 10%. LVEF decrease was observed in 9% (with tislelizumab) and 5% (chemotherapy only) of patients.
quarterly_data.figure: diarrhea 85% of 330 / 81% of 395 patients; serious adverse reactions 59% / 49%; discontinuation 13% / 10%; LVEF decrease 9% / 5%
